Rep. Miller’s push to align SNAP with actual nutrition is spot-on. Taxpayers shouldn’t foot the bill for junk food while diabetes rates explode. The Healthy SNAP Act’s focus on cutting sugary snacks and processed garbage from eligibility is a no-brainer—especially when you see $46K toilets and $15B rail boondoggles burning through budgets. 

USAID’s $2M for Guatemalan sex changes and State Dept-funded Ukrainian breakdancing prove bureaucrats prioritize woke pet projects over real needs. Redirecting SNAP funds to nutrient-dense foods forces accountability while tackling the obesity crisis. 

Let’s stop subsidizing poor health and start demanding efficiency—every dollar wasted on candy is a dollar stolen from veterans, border security, or deficit reduction.

@RepMaryMiller @SecRollins @SecKennedy The GOP is slashing SNAP in 2026—but now you’re pretending to care about nutrition? You defund food aid, block school lunches, and serve corporate junk while shaming the poor. This isn’t about health—it’s cruelty dressed up as policy.

SNAP’s original purpose was to fight hunger—not fund a junk food pipeline. The Nutritious SNAP Act of 2025 finally cracks down on taxpayer-funded soda, snacks, and desserts by redefining eligible food items. Section 2(a) explicitly bans nonalcoholic beverages except milk substitutes, water, and 100% juice.

Meanwhile, USDA data shows 20% of SNAP dollars go to sugary drinks and processed snacks. Obesity costs taxpayers $173B annually in medical bills.

Redirecting SNAP to nutrient-dense foods isn’t punitive—it’s fiscal sanity. Stop subsidizing Big Food’s profits with public health dollars.

See how the Nutritious SNAP Act rewrites the rules and what’s at stake: https://t.co/2ClHhgoIpm
